sections.body: Countries are governed in different ways. In a DEMOCRACY, citizens elect leaders. In a MONARCHY, a king or queen is head of state (often with an elected parliament too). In an AUTHORITARIAN system, power is held by one leader or party with limited elections or freedoms.

Many countries separate power into 3 branches: LEGISLATIVE (makes laws, such as a parliament), EXECUTIVE (runs the country, such as a president or prime minister) and JUDICIAL (courts that interpret laws).
Laws are usually proposed, debated, voted on, and then signed into law. Courts can check laws against a constitution.
People disagree about which policies are best. That's normal in a democracy. Look at the evidence and listen to different views.

quiz.q: Which branch of government makes laws?
hints: Parliaments and congresses belong to it.
Courts are judicial; presidents lead the executive. Who's left to make laws?
quiz.explain: The legislative branch (such as a parliament) makes laws.

options: So no single group has unchecked power
hints: What could go wrong if one person controlled everything?
In sport, players play, referees judge, and rule-makers write the rules. Why keep these separate?
quiz.explain: Separating powers lets each branch check the others, so no one has unchecked power.
